east-india-company.name: East India Company
east-india-company.summary: An English, later British, trading company founded in 1600 that grew to rule large parts of the Indian subcontinent, with its own armies, before dissolving in 1874.

bandel-cheese.name: Bandel cheese
bandel-cheese.summary: A smoked cheese originating in the former Portuguese colony of Bandel in eastern India, introduced and made under Portuguese supervision; today kept alive by very few remaining artisans.

sultanate-of-golconda.name: Qutb Shahi dynasty
sultanate-of-golconda.summary: Persianate, Shia Muslim ruling family of Turkoman origin that founded the Sultanate of Golconda in southern India in 1518, ending in 1687 under Mughal conquest.

nizam-of-hyderabad.name: Nizam of Hyderabad
nizam-of-hyderabad.summary: Title of the rulers of Hyderabad State in India, first held by Asaf Jah I from 1724, whose dynasty later accepted British suzerainty and ruled until 1948.

sivatattva-ratnakara.name: Sivatattva Ratnakara
sivatattva-ratnakara.summary: A 17th-century Sanskrit encyclopedia compiled by King Basavappa Nayaka of the Keladi Nayaka dynasty, written in verse across 108 chapters and about 13,000 stanzas.

khichdi.name: Khichdi
khichdi.summary: A South Asian dish of rice and lentils with many regional variations, often one of the first solid foods given to babies in parts of India.

vikram-samvat.name: Vikram Samvat
vikram-samvat.summary: A lunisolar calendar used across the Indian subcontinent and still official in Nepal, with an epoch of 57 BCE that puts its year count roughly 56 to 57 years ahead of the Gregorian calendar.

marwar.name: Marwar
marwar.summary: A historical and cultural region in western Rajasthan, India, also called the Jodhpur region, and the homeland of the Marwari language and trading community.

sojat.name: Sojat
sojat.summary: A city in Rajasthan's Pali district on the Sukri River, known today for its henna (mehendi) farms and production.

jahangir.name: Jahangir
jahangir.summary: Fourth Mughal emperor (r. 1605–1627), son of Akbar, whose reign combined artistic and architectural flourishing with political intrigue.

akbar.name: Akbar
akbar.summary: Third Mughal emperor, reigning from 1556 to 1605, who expanded and consolidated Mughal rule across the Indian subcontinent and brought Rajput rulers into the court through alliances and marriage.

shah-jahan.name: Shah Jahan
shah-jahan.summary: Fifth Mughal emperor, ruling from 1628 to 1658, whose reign marked the height of Mughal architecture and culture, including his commissioning of the Taj Mahal.

aurangzeb.name: Aurangzeb
aurangzeb.summary: Sixth Mughal emperor, reigning from 1658 to 1707, under whom the empire reached its greatest territorial extent.

badshahi-mosque.name: Badshahi Mosque
badshahi-mosque.summary: An imperial Mughal-era mosque in Lahore, Pakistan, built by Emperor Aurangzeb in 1671–1673, which remained the largest mosque in the world for over three centuries.

lahore-fort.name: Alamgiri Gate
lahore-fort.summary: The grand gate of Lahore Fort in Pakistan, built by the last major Mughal emperor, Aurangzeb, and facing the Badshahi Mosque.

wazir-khan-mosque.name: Wazir Khan Mosque
wazir-khan-mosque.summary: A 17th-century Mughal mosque in Lahore, built 1634 to 1641, celebrated as the most ornately decorated Mughal-era mosque for its tile-work and frescoes.

bibi-ka-maqbara.name: Bibi Ka Maqbara
bibi-ka-maqbara.summary: A tomb in Aurangabad, India, commissioned in 1660 by Mughal emperor Aurangzeb's son for his mother, resembling the Taj Mahal and sometimes called the 'Taj of the Deccan.'

company-style.name: Company style
company-style.summary: A hybrid Indo-European painting style made in British India, blending Rajput and Mughal traditions with Western perspective, produced by Indian artists for European patrons in the 18th and 19th centuries.

murshidabad.name: Murshidabad
murshidabad.summary: Town in West Bengal, India, that was capital of the Bengal Subah for seventy years and a prosperous 18th-century hub of banking, trade and art before its decline after 1757.

dravidian-architecture.name: Dravidian architecture
dravidian-architecture.summary: A South Indian temple-building style reaching its final form by the 16th century, marked by shorter, pyramidal towers over the sanctuary and, in larger temples, tall gateway towers.

vimana-architectural-feature.name: Vimana
vimana-architectural-feature.summary: The tower structure above the inner sanctum in South Indian and Odisha Hindu temples, usually pyramid-shaped and, in South India, typically smaller than the temple's grand gatehouses.

shikhara.name: Shikhara
shikhara.summary: The rising tower over the shrine chamber in North Indian Hindu (and some Jain) temple architecture, whose name means 'mountain peak' in Sanskrit.

bishandas.name: Bishan Das
bishandas.summary: An Indian court painter under the Mughal emperor Jahangir, renowned for realistic portraits, who traveled to Persia in 1613 to paint Shah Abbas I and other Persian nobles.

manohar-das.name: Manohar Das
manohar-das.summary: An Indian Hindu court painter in the Mughal style, active from about 1582 to 1624, who painted for Emperor Akbar and later his son Jahangir, depicting royal life.

abu-l-hasan-artist.name: Abu al-Hasan
abu-l-hasan-artist.summary: Mughal miniature painter from Delhi (1589 – c. 1630) who worked during the reign of Emperor Jahangir.

govardhan-artist.name: Govardhan
govardhan-artist.summary: Mughal-era Indian painter (active 1595–1640) known for rich, sensuous colour, who illustrated the Baburnama and produced portraits now held in American and European museum collections.

daulat-artist.name: Daulat
daulat-artist.summary: A leading Mughal court painter active from about 1595 to the 1630s under emperors Akbar, Jahangir and Shah Jahan, who began with narrative scenes and portraits before specializing in ornate miniature borders.

shah-jahan-mosque-thatta.name: Shah Jahan Mosque, Thatta
shah-jahan-mosque-thatta.summary: A 17th-century congregational mosque in Thatta, Pakistan, built under Shah Jahan and considered to have South Asia's most elaborate tile-work.

chaukhandi-tombs.name: Chaukhandi tombs
chaukhandi-tombs.summary: An early Islamic cemetery in eastern Karachi, Pakistan, known for elaborate sandstone carvings in the funerary style typical of lower Sindh.

battle-of-khanwa.name: Battle of Khanwa
battle-of-khanwa.summary: 1527 battle in which Babur's Mughal forces defeated Rana Sanga's Kingdom of Mewar for control of northern India, among the first battles there to use gunpowder.

babur.name: Babur
babur.summary: Founder of the Mughal Empire in South Asia (1483–1530), a descendant of Timur and Genghis Khan who conquered Kabul in 1504 and defeated the Sultan of Delhi in 1526.

rana-sanga.name: Rana Sanga
rana-sanga.summary: Ruler of Mewar from 1509 to 1528 whose realm, at its height in 1521, stretched from Malwa to the Indus River; he fought Babur's Mughal forces before being defeated at Khanwa, largely due to Babur's use of gunpowder.

mewar.name: Mewar
mewar.summary: A historical region in south-eastern Rajasthan, India, covering the Udaipur, Rajsamand, Bhilwara, Chittorgarh and Pratapgarh districts, where Mewari is spoken as a shared language.

first-luso-malabarese-war.name: First Luso-Malabarese War
first-luso-malabarese-war.summary: First armed conflict fought by the Portuguese Empire in Asia, beginning in 1500 over trade with the Zamorin of Calicut and lasting thirteen years.

zamorin.name: Zamorin of Calicut
zamorin.summary: Title of the rulers of the Calicut kingdom in South Malabar, India, who built Calicut into a major trading port; the last Zamorin died by suicide after territory nearby fell to Hyder Ali.

afonso-de-albuquerque.name: Afonso de Albuquerque
afonso-de-albuquerque.summary: Portuguese general and admiral who served as viceroy of Portuguese India from 1509 to 1515, conquering Goa and leading the first European raids into the Persian Gulf and Red Sea.

nader-shah.name: Nader Shah
nader-shah.summary: Founder of Iran's Afsharid dynasty, ruling as shah from 1736 until his assassination in 1747; his campaigns built an empire stretching from India to the Caucasus.

battle-of-karnal.name: Battle of Karnal
battle-of-karnal.summary: 1739 battle in which Nader Shah's forces crushed the Mughal army in three hours, opening the way to the sack of Delhi and critically weakening the Mughal Empire.

peacock-throne.name: Peacock Throne
peacock-throne.summary: The bejeweled imperial throne of the Mughal emperors, commissioned by Shah Jahan in the early 1600s and named for its mounted peacock figures, until Nader Shah carried it off as a war trophy in 1739.

ahmad-shah-durrani.name: Ahmad Shah Durrani
ahmad-shah-durrani.summary: Founder of the Durrani Empire and often regarded as founder of modern Afghanistan, who led campaigns for over 25 years from about 1747 across West, Central and South Asia, including sacking Delhi in 1757 and defeating the Marathas at the Third Battle of Panipat.

sialkot.name: Sialkot
sialkot.summary: City in Punjab, Pakistan, believed to succeed the ancient city of Sagala, later capital of the Indo-Greek kingdom under Menander I and a major center of Islamic scholarship under the Mughals.

lodi-dynasty.name: Lodi dynasty
lodi-dynasty.summary: The royal family that ruled the Sultanate of Delhi from 1451 to 1526, the fifth and final dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, founded by Bahlul Lodi.

first-battle-of-panipat.name: First Battle of Panipat
first-battle-of-panipat.summary: Battle fought on 21 April 1526 in which Babur, using gunpowder weapons, defeated Ibrahim Lodi, the Sultan of Delhi, marking the start of Mughal rule in India.

louren-o-de-almeida.name: Lourenço de Almeida
louren-o-de-almeida.summary: Portuguese explorer and military commander (c. 1480–1508), son of the first viceroy of Portuguese India, who made Ceylon tributary to Portugal before dying in the Battle of Chaul.

chaul.name: Chaul
chaul.summary: A village in Maharashtra, India, that was once a town of Portuguese India.

battle-of-chaul.name: Battle of Chaul
battle-of-chaul.summary: An 1508 naval battle between Portuguese and Egyptian Mamluk forces off India, ending in a Mamluk victory and the first Portuguese defeat at sea in the Indian Ocean.

bajirao-i.name: Bajirao I
bajirao-i.summary: The seventh Peshwa (prime minister) of the Maratha Empire (1700–1740), known for defeating the Nizam of Hyderabad and leading the Battle of Delhi in 1737, seen as the pinnacle of his military career.

carnatic-wars.name: Carnatic Wars
carnatic-wars.summary: A series of mid-18th-century conflicts in India's coastal Carnatic region in which Britain's East India Company outmaneuvered its French rival, paving the way for the British Raj.

battle-of-plassey.name: Battle of Plassey
battle-of-plassey.summary: A 23 June 1757 battle in which Robert Clive's British East India Company forces defeated Bengal's Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah, aided by the betrayal of his commander Mir Jafar, paving the way for British control of Bengal.

ibrahim-khan-lodi.name: Ibrahim Lodi
ibrahim-khan-lodi.summary: The last Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate and of the Lodi dynasty, reigning from 1517 until 1526, when Babur defeated and killed him at the First Battle of Panipat, opening the way for the Mughal Empire.

krishnadevaraya.name: Krishnadevaraya
krishnadevaraya.summary: Emperor of the Vijayanagara Empire from 1509 to 1529, widely regarded as one of the greatest rulers in Indian history, who expanded the empire to its political and cultural peak.

vijayanagara-empire.name: Vijayanagara Empire
vijayanagara-empire.summary: Founded in 1336 by brothers Harihara I and Bukka Raya I, this Hindu empire ruled much of Southern India and was named after its capital city, now the ruined UNESCO site of Hampi.

vasco-da-gama.name: Vasco da Gama
vasco-da-gama.summary: Portuguese explorer (c. 1460s-1524) whose 1497-1499 voyage opened the first sea route from Europe to India around Africa's Cape of Good Hope.

pedro-lvares-cabral.name: Pedro Álvares Cabral
pedro-lvares-cabral.summary: Portuguese nobleman and navigator (c. 1467–c. 1520) regarded as the European discoverer of Brazil, leading a 1500 expedition that touched four continents.

francisco-de-almeida.name: Francisco de Almeida
francisco-de-almeida.summary: Portuguese nobleman and soldier (c. 1450–1510), the first governor and viceroy of Portuguese India, who established Portuguese dominance in the Indian Ocean with his 1509 victory at the Battle of Diu.

duarte-pacheco-pereira.name: Duarte Pacheco Pereira
duarte-pacheco-pereira.summary: A Portuguese sea captain, explorer and cartographer (c. 1460–1533), nicknamed the "Portuguese Achilles" for his exceptional skill in warfare, navigation, mathematics and astronomy.

banda-singh-bahadur.name: Banda Singh Bahadur
banda-singh-bahadur.summary: A Sikh military commander (1670–1716) who led the Khalsa Army against the Mughal Empire, sacked Samana in 1709, abolished feudal land rule in Punjab, and was captured and killed by the Mughals.

chhatrasal.name: Chhatrasal
chhatrasal.summary: Bundela ruler of Panna and Bundelkhand from 1675 to 1731, known for resisting Mughal rule and leading Bundelkhand's struggle for independence.

bundela.name: Bundela Rajputs
bundela.summary: Rajput clan that ruled large parts of Bundelkhand in medieval times, whose cadet lineages founded several states in the region from the 16th century.

panna-state.name: Panna State
panna-state.summary: A kingdom and later princely state of colonial India in what is now Madhya Pradesh, named after its capital town, Panna.

vadda-ghallughara.name: Vadda Ghallughara
vadda-ghallughara.summary: A massacre of thousands of Sikhs by Afghan Durrani forces in the Punjab region in February 1762, part of a decades-long campaign against the Sikhs.

maldeo-rathore.name: Maldeo Rathore
maldeo-rathore.summary: King of the Rathore dynasty who ruled Marwar from 1532, conquering large territories across Rajasthan and neighboring regions while refusing alliance with the Sur or Mughal Empires.

chittorgarh.name: Chittorgarh
chittorgarh.summary: A city in Rajasthan, India, and former stronghold of the Rajput state of Mewar, whose fort was sacked in 1303, 1535 and 1568.

guru-nanak.name: Guru Nanak
guru-nanak.summary: An Indian spiritual teacher and poet (1469–1539) regarded as the founder of Sikhism and the first of its ten Gurus, who taught belief in one God and equality.

janamsakhis.name: Janamsakhi
janamsakhis.summary: Hagiographies of Guru Nanak, the founder of Sikhism, drawn from oral tradition mixing fact, homily and legend; the earliest were composed 50 to 80 years after his death.

bhai-bala.name: Bhai Bala
bhai-bala.summary: Believed by some to have been a companion of Guru Nanak (1466 to 1544) and a close associate of Bhai Mardana.

indian-style-poetry.name: Sabk-i Hindi
indian-style-poetry.summary: A Persian poetry style associated with poets at Indian courts in the Mughal era, sometimes also called sabk-i Isfahani or sabk-i Safavi after similarly styled Safavid-court poets.

dean-mahomed.name: Dean Mahomed
dean-mahomed.summary: British Indian traveller, soldier, surgeon and entrepreneur (1759-1851) who introduced Indian cuisine and shampoo baths to Europe and was one of the earliest notable non-European immigrants to the West.

vaishnavism.name: Vaishnavism
vaishnavism.summary: A major Hindu religious tradition that reveres Vishnu as the supreme being, including sub-traditions worshipping his avatars Krishna and Rama.

kalidasa.name: Kalidasa
kalidasa.summary: A Classical Sanskrit poet and playwright of the 4th–5th century CE, often considered ancient India's greatest poet, whose surviving works are based on Hindu Puranas and philosophy.

mahakavya.name: Sargabandha
mahakavya.summary: A genre of ornate Indian court epic poetry in Classical Sanskrit, also called mahakavya, marked by elaborate descriptions of scenery, love and battle, developed from the Mahabharata and Ramayana.

nilakantha-somayaji.name: Nilakantha Somayaji
nilakantha-somayaji.summary: Indian mathematician and astronomer of the Kerala school (1444–1544) whose Tantrasamgraha (1500–1501) revised planetary models and whose commentary discussed infinite series for pi.

kerala-school-of-astronomy-and-mathemati.name: Kerala school of astronomy and mathematics
kerala-school-of-astronomy-and-mathemati.summary: A school of mathematics and astronomy founded by Madhava of Sangamagrama in Kerala, India, active from the 14th to 16th centuries, known for discovering early power series for trigonometric functions before calculus was invented in Europe.
kerala-school-of-astronomy-and-mathemati.source_title: Kerala school of astronomy and mathematics

aryabhata.name: Aryabhata
aryabhata.summary: Indian mathematician-astronomer (476–550 CE), among the first of the classical era's great scholars, known for the Aryabhatiya and Arya-siddhanta.

tantrasamgraha.name: Tantrasamgraha
tantrasamgraha.summary: An astronomical treatise completed in 1501 CE by Nilakantha Somayaji of the Kerala school, revising planetary models for Mercury and Venus.

johannes-kepler.name: Johannes Kepler
johannes-kepler.summary: German astronomer and mathematician (1571–1630) whose laws of planetary motion made him a key figure of the Scientific Revolution; he worked under Tycho Brahe and later as imperial mathematician to Emperor Rudolf II.

thanjavur.name: Thanjavur
thanjavur.summary: A city in Tamil Nadu, India, and former Chola capital, home to the UNESCO-listed Brihadisvara Temple built by Emperor Rajaraja I and known for its distinctive Tanjore painting style.

dhaka.name: Dhaka (Dacca)
dhaka.summary: Former name of Dhaka, now the capital of Bangladesh; it grew from the 17th century as a Mughal provincial capital and trading hub, once one of the world's most prosperous cities.

bijapur.name: Bijapur
bijapur.summary: A city in Karnataka, India, known for historical monuments built under the Adil Shahi dynasty, which ruled the city after the Bahmani Sultanate split.

ga-e-a-daivaj-a.name: Gaṇeśa Daivajña
ga-e-a-daivaj-a.summary: Sixteenth-century Indian astronomer, astrologer and mathematician, born around 1507, who wrote works on predicting eclipses, calendar calculations, and an approximation of pi.

grahalaghava.name: Grahalaghava
grahalaghava.summary: A 16th-century Sanskrit astronomical treatise by Gaṇeśa Daivajna, used as a handbook for computing planetary positions and considered the most popular such text among Indian calendar-makers.

malwa.name: Malwa
malwa.summary: Historical volcanic-plateau region of west-central India, ruled by successive kingdoms since ancient times and later known for saltpeter production used in gunpowder.

kozhikode.name: Calicut
kozhikode.summary: Historic port city on India's Malabar Coast, capital of the Samoothiri (Zamorin) kingdom, visited in medieval times by Marco Polo, Ibn Battuta, Zheng He and Vasco da Gama.

diu-india.name: Diu
diu-india.summary: Medieval fortified fishing town in India, known for its fortress and old Portuguese cathedral, located on Diu Island.

chhapra.name: Chhapra
chhapra.summary: A city in Bihar, India, near the confluence of the Ghaghara and Ganges rivers, once used as a center of saltpeter refining for gunpowder.

timurid-dynasty.name: Timurid dynasty
timurid-dynasty.summary: The Turco-Mongol ruling family of the Timurid Empire, descended from Timur, whose members also founded the Mughal Empire and called themselves Gurkani, meaning 'son-in-law'.

fergana-valley.name: Fergana Valley
fergana-valley.summary: Fertile Central Asian valley spanning parts of modern Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan, a historic crossroads of Greek, Chinese, Bactrian and Parthian civilizations and homeland of Mughal founder Babur.

deccan-sultanates.name: Deccan sultanates
deccan-sultanates.summary: Five Persianate Muslim kingdoms that arose on the Deccan Plateau after the Bahmani Sultanate broke apart in the late 15th century; they later allied to defeat the Vijayanagara Empire in 1565.

gajapati-empire.name: Gajapati Empire
gajapati-empire.summary: A medieval Hindu kingdom centered on Odisha that ruled from about 1434 to 1541, at its height stretching from West Bengal to Tamil Nadu and rivaling the Vijayanagara Empire.

battle-of-talikota.name: Battle of Talikota
battle-of-talikota.summary: A battle fought on 23 January 1565 in which an alliance of Deccan sultanates defeated the Vijayanagara Empire, a defeat that led to the empire's eventual collapse and reshaped Deccan politics.

mansabdar.name: Mansabdar
mansabdar.summary: The Mughal Empire's system of graded military-administrative ranks fixing an officer's pay, precedence, and required cavalry, fusing army, nobility and civil service into one hierarchy under Akbar.

bahadur-shah-i.name: Bahadur Shah I
bahadur-shah-i.summary: The eighth Mughal emperor, ruling 1707 to 1712, who defeated his brother Azam Shah's rival claim to the throne after Aurangzeb's death; his reign faced revolts by Rajputs and Sikhs.

sayyid-brothers.name: Sayyid brothers
sayyid-brothers.summary: Abdullah Khan II and Syed Hussain Ali Khan, two powerful Mughal nobles who became de facto rulers of the empire after 1707, seating and deposing emperors at will.

siraj-ud-daulah.name: Siraj-ud-Daulah
siraj-ud-daulah.summary: The last independent Nawab of Bengal (1733–1757), whose defeat at the Battle of Plassey in 1757 marked the start of East India Company rule over Bengal.

nawabs-of-bengal.name: Nawab of Bengal
nawabs-of-bengal.summary: Title of the hereditary rulers of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa under Mughal India, who governed as effectively independent monarchs from Murshidabad while still issuing coins in the Mughal emperor's name.

mir-jafar.name: Mir Jafar
mir-jafar.summary: Commander-in-chief who betrayed Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah at the Battle of Plassey in 1757 and became the first Nawab of Bengal dependent on the East India Company.

buxar.name: Buxar
buxar.summary: A city in the Indian state of Bihar, site of the 1764 Battle of Buxar.

shah-alam-ii.name: Shah Alam II
shah-alam-ii.summary: Seventeenth Mughal emperor (1728–1806) whose reign saw invasions by Ahmad Shah Abdali, defeat at the Battle of Buxar in 1764, and the eventual British capture of Delhi.

dewan.name: Diwan
dewan.summary: A powerful government official, minister, or ruler in Mughal and post-Mughal India, often head of a state institution of the same name.

third-battle-of-panipat.name: Third Battle of Panipat
third-battle-of-panipat.summary: A massive 1761 battle near Delhi between the Maratha Empire and the invading Durrani Empire, won by the Afghans with heavy fatalities on both sides.

marthanda-varma.name: Marthanda Varma
marthanda-varma.summary: Founding monarch of the Kingdom of Travancore in southern India, reigning 1729–1758, remembered for defeating Dutch East India Company forces at the Battle of Colachel in 1741.

travancore.name: Travancore
travancore.summary: A princely state in southern India lasting from about 1729 to 1949, ruled by the Travancore royal family and covering most of the southern part of modern Kerala.

battle-of-colachel.name: Battle of Colachel
battle-of-colachel.summary: An 1741 battle in which the Indian kingdom of Travancore, under King Marthanda Varma, defeated the Dutch East India Company's forces.

treaty-of-mavelikkara.name: Treaty of Mavelikkara
treaty-of-mavelikkara.summary: 1753 treaty of peace and friendship between Maharajah Marthanda Varma of Travancore and the Dutch, setting out trade and military-supply terms.

navya-ny-ya.name: Navya-Nyāya
navya-ny-ya.summary: A 'new reason' school of Indian logic and philosophy founded in the 13th century by Gaṅgeśa, refining earlier Nyāya thought and remaining active into the 18th century.

raghunatha-shiromani.name: Raghunatha Shiromani
raghunatha-shiromani.summary: Indian philosopher and logician (c. 1477–1547), head of the ancient Mithila University, who brought the Navya Nyaya school of logic to its analytical peak.

vallabha.name: Vallabha
vallabha.summary: Indian philosopher (1478-1530) who founded the Krishna-centered Pushtimarg sect of Vaishnavism and promoted devotion to Krishna over an ascetic life.

shuddhadvaita.name: Shuddhadvaita
shuddhadvaita.summary: A 'purely non-dual' Hindu philosophy founded by Vallabha (1479–1531), centered on devotion to Krishna within the Pushtimarga tradition of Vaishnavism.

nyaya.name: Nyaya
nyaya.summary: One of six orthodox schools of Hindu philosophy, whose name means 'justice' or 'method,' known for its systematic theories of logic and epistemology.

vaisheshika.name: Vaisheshika
vaisheshika.summary: One of the six classical schools of Hindu philosophy from ancient India, known for developing an atomist theory of the physical universe.

samkhya.name: Samkhya
samkhya.summary: A dualistic school of Hindu philosophy holding that reality consists of two principles: consciousness (Purusha) and matter or nature (Prakriti).

m-m-s.name: Mīmāṃsā
m-m-s.summary: One of six orthodox schools of Hindu philosophy, focused on interpreting Vedic ritual texts; it later influenced the Vedānta tradition.

yashovijaya.name: Yashovijaya
yashovijaya.summary: A 17th-century Jain philosopher-monk (1624-1688) and prolific writer with lasting influence on Jainism, a disciple in the lineage of Jain monk Hiravijaya, who influenced the Mughal Emperor Akbar to give up eating meat.

dara-shikoh.name: Dara Shikoh
dara-shikoh.summary: Eldest son and heir of Mughal emperor Shah Jahan, defeated by his brother Aurangzeb in a war of succession and executed in 1659; noted for promoting harmony between Islamic and Hindu thought.

raja-ram-mohan-roy.name: Ram Mohan Roy
raja-ram-mohan-roy.summary: Indian social reformer and writer (1772–1833), a founder of the Brahmo Sabha reform movement, dubbed the 'Father of the Indian Renaissance' for campaigning against sati and child marriage.

samarth-ramdas.name: Samarth Ramdas
samarth-ramdas.summary: An Indian Hindu saint, philosopher and poet who lived from about 1608 to 1682 and was a devotee of the gods Rama and Hanuman.

dasbodh.name: Dasbodh
dasbodh.summary: A 1654 Marathi spiritual text of devotion and insight, narrated by the saint Samarth Ramdas to his disciple Kalyan Swami, offering guidance on religious and daily life.

nana-dharmadhikari.name: Nana Dharmadhikari
nana-dharmadhikari.summary: Indian spiritual master and social reformer (1922–2008) who founded a movement against superstition and orthodox customs, later given Maharashtra's highest civilian award.

stika-and-n-stika.name: Āstika and nāstika
stika-and-n-stika.summary: Terms scholars use to classify schools of Indian philosophy: āstika schools accept the Vedas as authoritative, while nāstika schools do not.

johan-zoffany.name: Johann Zoffany
johan-zoffany.summary: German neoclassical painter (1733–1810) active mainly in England, Italy and India, whose works hang in major collections including the National Gallery and the Royal Collection.

tilly-kettle.name: Tilly Kettle
tilly-kettle.summary: English portrait painter (1735–1786) and the first British artist to work in colonial India.

william-hodges.name: William Hodges
william-hodges.summary: English painter (1744–1797) who joined James Cook's second Pacific voyage, known for paintings of places he visited including Tahiti, Easter Island and New Zealand.

thomas-daniell.name: Thomas Daniell
thomas-daniell.summary: An English landscape painter (1749–1840) known for Orientalist themes, who spent seven years in India with his nephew William and published aquatint series of the country.

william-daniell.name: William Daniell
william-daniell.summary: English painter and printmaker (1769–1837) specialising in landscape and marine art, who travelled in India with his uncle Thomas Daniell to produce Oriental Scenery, and later painted Britain's coastline.

gingee-fort.name: Gingee Fort
gingee-fort.summary: Hilltop fortress in Tamil Nadu, India, called the "Troy of the East" by the British; built from around the 11th century and later held by Marathas, Bijapur sultans, Mughals, the French and the British.

bukhara.name: Bukhara
bukhara.summary: Ancient Silk Road city in what is now Uzbekistan, a major center of Islamic scholarship and birthplace of Imam Bukhari, later capital of the Emirate of Bukhara until 1920.

tabriz.name: Tabriz
tabriz.summary: A city in northwestern Iran and capital of East Azerbaijan province, historically also known as Tauris, noted today for its handicrafts and carpet weaving.

shiraz.name: Shiraz
shiraz.summary: Iran's fifth-most-populous city and capital of Fars province, a regional trade center for over a thousand years and home to the poets Hafez and Saadi.
